headline: Ancient painted tomb uncovered near Egypt's Luxor

sources.title: Archaeologists uncover 3,000-year-old tomb near Egypt's Luxor
3,000-year-old tomb of ancient Egyptian official Paser discovered in Luxor's Theban Necropolis
3,000-year-old Egyptian tomb with vivid afterlife paintings uncovered near Luxor

chunks.text: Archaeologists in Egypt have {{dug up}} an [[ancient]] [[tomb]] near the city of Luxor. A Dutch team from Leiden University {{teamed up with}} Egypt's [[antiquities]] authority to [[explore]] the west bank of the Nile. The tomb is about 3,000 years old, and it [[belonged to]] an [[official]] named Paser. Experts believe it {{dates back}} to the Ramesside period, a great age of Egyptian [[pharaohs]].

verbs.correct: To bring something out of the ground by digging
verbs.wrong: To search old records in order to find hidden facts
verbs.why: Archaeologists dig up ancient pottery, and workers sometimes dig up old pipes during construction. In Egypt, a team recently dug up a 3,000-year-old tomb near the city of Luxor.

verbs.correct: To join with someone to work together
verbs.wrong: To reach someone who is ahead of you
verbs.why: A local school might team up with a museum for a field trip, and a small charity can team up with a bigger group for funding. A Dutch team from Leiden University teamed up with Egypt's antiquities authority to explore the site.

verbs.correct: To have existed since a particular time in the past
verbs.wrong: To be old-fashioned and no longer in style
verbs.why: This old church dates back two hundred years, and some family recipes date back several generations. Experts believe the newly found tomb dates back to the Ramesside period of ancient Egypt.

chunks.text: What makes the tomb special is that its walls still {{show off}} [[colorful]] painted scenes. Time has not {{worn away}} the bright images, which show Paser worshiping the gods inside sacred [[shrines]]. Another painting shows him seated [[beside]] his wife, in front of a table [[piled with]] [[offerings]]. The art really {{leaps out}} because its colors have [[lasted]] for more than 3,000 years.

verbs.correct: To display something proudly for people to see
verbs.wrong: To behave in a boastful way to get attention
verbs.why: A gallery shows off new paintings, and a jeweler shows off a rare gem in the front window. The walls of Paser's tomb still show off bright, colorful scenes after 3,000 years.

verbs.correct: To slowly damage or remove something over time
verbs.wrong: To make something look shiny and new again
verbs.why: Rain slowly wears away stone, and years of sun wear away paint on an old house. Time has not worn away the bright colors inside Paser's tomb, which still look fresh today.

verbs.correct: To be very noticeable and catch the eye at once
verbs.wrong: To appear suddenly from a hidden place
verbs.why: A bright headline leaps out from a newspaper page, and a bold color leaps out in a quiet room. The painted scenes in Paser's tomb leap out because their colors have lasted more than 3,000 years.

chunks.text: The team did not {{come across}} the tomb [[by luck]]. They have worked at this [[site]] since 2018, and this season their [[careful]] [[digging]] finally {{paid off}}. As they {{cleared away}} sand and fallen stone, a [[courtyard]], a rock [[chapel]], and underground [[burial chambers]] slowly appeared.

verbs.correct: To find or meet something by chance
verbs.wrong: To change your opinion and agree
verbs.why: You might come across an old letter while cleaning, or come across a rare coin in the garden. This team did not come across the tomb by luck, since they had worked at the site since 2018.

verbs.correct: To bring a good result after a lot of effort
verbs.wrong: To finish repaying money that you owe
verbs.why: Years of hard training can pay off with a big win, and patience often pays off in the end. This season, the team's careful digging finally paid off with the discovery of Paser's tomb.

verbs.correct: To remove things to leave a clean, empty space
verbs.wrong: To add more sand and stone to a structure
verbs.why: Workers clear away snow after a storm, and volunteers clear away trash after a big event. The team cleared away sand and fallen stone until a courtyard and burial chambers slowly appeared.

chunks.text: News of the find has [[drawn attention]] [[from around the world]]. Officials hope the painted walls will {{shed light on}} Paser's life and his [[exact]] role in Egyptian society. Researchers still need to {{pore over}} the writing on the walls to learn his full [[titles]]. The discovery is [[a reminder of]] how much history still [[lies buried]] under Luxor's sands.

verbs.correct: To give new information that helps explain something
verbs.wrong: To give final proof that something is definitely true
verbs.why: New evidence can shed light on an old mystery, and a diary can shed light on a person's private life. Officials hope the painted walls will shed light on Paser's exact role in Egyptian society.

verbs.correct: To read or study something very carefully
verbs.wrong: To photograph a surface in fine detail
verbs.why: Historians pore over old letters, and lawyers pore over documents late into the night. Researchers still need to pore over the writing on the tomb walls to learn Paser's full titles.

mainIdea.s: A Dutch team and Egypt's antiquities authority dug up a 3,000-year-old tomb near Luxor. It belonged to a senior ancient official, and its walls have kept their bright colors.
mainIdea.why: A Dutch team from Leiden University worked with Egypt's antiquities authority to dig up the tomb of a senior ancient official. Its walls still show bright painted scenes after 3,000 years.

mainIdea.s: The team found the tomb by pure luck on their very first visit to this ancient site. They have already read every word painted on the walls to learn the official's exact titles.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the team had worked at the site since 2018, so it was not sudden luck. Researchers still need to pore over the wall writing to learn the official's exact titles.

mainIdea.s: Near Cairo, a separate team recently opened an unrelated chamber sealed for centuries. Inside, they found stone tools and pottery that once belonged to ordinary workers.
mainIdea.why: This is about a different, unrelated chamber found near Cairo that held tools and pottery. It has nothing to do with the painted tomb near Luxor.

lines.text: Archaeologists near Luxor have {{dug up}} a painted tomb that's 3,000 years old.
That's the amazing part. Time hasn't {{worn away}} the colors. The walls still {{show off}} bright scenes of an official named Paser worshiping the gods.
[[Imagine that]]. Three thousand years and the paint survives.
There's even a scene of him beside his wife, with a table of offerings. Researchers say the art really {{leaps out}} at you.
A Dutch team from Leiden University. They {{teamed up with}} Egypt's antiquities authority and have worked at the site since 2018.
So they didn't just {{come across}} it by luck?
Not at all. Years of careful digging finally {{paid off}}. As they {{cleared away}} sand and fallen stone, a courtyard, a chapel, and burial chambers appeared.
It {{dates back}} to the Ramesside period, the great age of the pharaohs.
Experts will {{pore over}} the writing on the walls. They hope it will {{shed light on}} Paser's life and his role in Egyptian society.
[[Who knows]] what else is still under those sands.
